items.title: Negaunee tightens rules to keep data centers out of most zones
items.dek: Council voted 7-0 to advance an ordinance confining data centers to mining and industrial areas, capping noise, height and emissions, with a public hearing set for Aug. 13.
items.source: Negaunee City Council or Planning Commission agenda
items.findings: Ordinance limits data centers to mining and industrial zones | Sets acceptable levels of noise disturbance and maximum building heights | Requires any air pollution, dust, smoke, glare, exhaust, noise, heat, vibration or humidity to be imperceptible at or beyond the property line | Negaunee City Council voted 7-0 to approve first reading and schedule Aug. 13 public hearing | Planning Commission drafted and recommended the ordinance | Michigan state law outlaws exclusionary zoning, preventing municipalities from completely outlawing specific lawful land-uses including data centers
items.perspective: Negaunee City Council approved the first reading 7-0 at its July meeting after the Planning Commission recommended the ordinance. Councilperson Jon Becker said he brought the issue to the planning commission and personally hopes the ordinance is restrictive enough that data centers choose to go elsewhere. Councilperson Amanda Ghanavati said she hopes it makes it nearly impossible for data centers
items.judge_note: Negaunee council voted 7-0 to advance a restrictive ordinance with a scheduled public hearing—a real decision and next step.

items.title: East Lansing extends data center moratorium to March 2027 to develop regulations
items.dek: City Council voted unanimously to prolong the pause, allowing more time for a work group to finalize guidelines amid growing concerns over large-scale projects.
items.judge_note: New council vote extending East Lansing's moratorium to a specific new date (March 2027), a concrete decision distinct from the earlier aquifer-focused pause.
